🚶 Walk Ancient Ur — Paternoster Row

A residential street in Ur (southern Iraq), c. 2000–1800 BCE, rebuilt from Woolley's AH quarter. Click “Start walking”, then look with the mouse and move with W A S D (or arrow keys). Shift = hurry, Esc = release mouse.

New: the West Gate stands open at the end of this very street — follow the Processional Way north, past the braziers, into the Ziggurat's sacred precinct (stops 17–18) along a walled avenue with houses to explore. And the Ziggurat itself is now climbable: up the triple staircases, around every terrace, into Nanna's shrine at the top (stop 19). Now with firelight and sound: braziers burn along the way, and with sound on you'll hear wind, birds, a distant lyre, fire crackle and your own footsteps.

New: Space = jump (hop onto stalls, steps and low roofs), the whole quarter is ringed by a city wall with six closed gates — and the city goes on beyond it — and the donkey walks his rounds with his handler, like the people.

The panel hides under the ☰ button while you walk — tap it any time to bring the panel back. You can walk up steps now: into the chapel, up No. 3's roof stairs, and down into its below-street rooms. The people of Ur walk their own errands, too.

Walk into No. 3 (the open doorway opposite the shops), visit the corner chapel, and follow the numbered stops ①–⑫. Press O for a bird's-eye orbit view, Walk to return.
